title: Smartagri DTPB FTP UGM Researchers Participate in the 2026 National Agrotropikal Seminar
author: Fahmi Arsyad
excerpt: Eight researchers from Smartagri UGM participated in the 2026 National Agrotropikal Seminar (Universitas Mulawarman, April 30), presenting eight studies spanning precision irrigation, IoT-based systems, UAV remote sensing, deep learning, and electrical impedance sensing. The participation underscores Smartagri's commitment to disseminating data-driven agricultural research and strengthening national academic networks in smart farming.
body:
**Yogyakarta, April 30, 2026** — The research team of the Smart Agriculture Research Center (Smartagri), Department of Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering (DTPB), Faculty of Agricultural Technology, Universitas Gadjah Mada (FTP UGM), participated in the 2026 National Agrotropikal Seminar organized by the Faculty of Agriculture, Universitas Mulawarman. The event was held online via Zoom Meeting on Thursday, April 30, 2026, under the theme _"Transformation of Agricultural Technology and Innovation for Food Security and Sustainable Agriculture."_

This participation involved eight Smartagri researchers: Ardan Desta Vaunendra, Devi Ramdani, Rizqi Asy'ari Ramadhan, Bagus Dwi Putra Atmaja, Arinda Fadea Pramaesela, Faiz Ridwan Pratama, Les' Aullian Achmad Argito, and M. Ilham Al Marda — all contributing to the dissemination of research findings and the strengthening of academic networks in precision agriculture and smart farming. The seminar featured keynote speakers and resource persons from various universities across Indonesia, discussing advancements in agricultural technology and innovation with a focus on digital technology integration, production system efficiency, and sustainability strategies in addressing global food security challenges.

![](/brand/uploads/30-4-2.webp) ![](/brand/uploads/30-4-3.webp)

During the event, the Smartagri research team presented a range of studies focusing on the application of data-driven precision agriculture technology and smart systems to improve production efficiency and resource management. The studies presented included:

- _Evaluation of Sprinkler Irrigation Implementation through Hydraulic Analysis and Water Distribution Uniformity Based on Christiansen Uniformity at Pantai Glagah Farmland, Kulon Progo_ — by Devi Ramdani
- _Development of an IoT-Based Automatic Sprinkler Irrigation System on Sandy Coastal Land_ — by Rizqi Asy'ari Ramadhan
- _Development of a Fuzzy Logic Algorithm for Sandy Soil Irrigation Optimization Based on Evapotranspiration and Soil Moisture_ — by Ardan Desta Vaunendra
- _Estimation of Rice Stomatal Conductance Using an XGBoost Algorithm Based on UAV Multispectral Imagery_ — by Faiz Ridwan Pratama
- _Development of a Deep Learning-Based Primary Channel Discharge Prediction Model to Support Cropping Pattern Optimization in the Sapon Irrigation Area, Kulon Progo Regency_ — by Bagus Dwi Putra Atmaja
- _Quantification of External Factors as a Basis for Operator Performance Evaluation in the Sapon Irrigation Area_ — by Arinda Fadea Pramaesela
- _Electrical Impedance Characteristics of Lettuce Leaves at 0.4 V and 100 kΩ_ — by Les' Aullian Achmad Argito
- _Machine Learning-Based Classification of Papaya Plant Health from Leaf Physiological Data_ — by Muhammad Ilham Al Marda

The research approaches emphasized the integration of technologies such as remote sensing, data-driven control systems, the Internet of Things (IoT), and machine learning-based modeling to support decision-making in the modern agricultural sector. These studies form part of the broader development of precision agriculture technologies aimed at improving water use efficiency, optimizing irrigation systems, and enhancing agricultural productivity in a sustainable manner.

The students involved in this research were supervised by Dr. Murtiningrum and Dr. Andri Prima Nugroho from the Smart Agriculture Research Center, Department of Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering, Faculty of Agricultural Technology, Universitas Gadjah Mada. The research activities were funded through the Priority Research Downstream Program – SINERGI, Ministry of Education, Culture, Research, and Technology 2025. Additionally, the research was supported by the Working Group Food Security (WGFS 1.2) — Precision Agriculture and Smart Farming, under the Center of Excellence Among Universities (PUAPT) Universitas Gadjah Mada, which provided research facility support.

This participation in the seminar reflects the Smart Agriculture Research Center's commitment to developing research relevant to the needs of the modern agricultural sector, while also serving as a platform for exchanging ideas, expanding collaboration, and strengthening contributions toward sustainable agricultural development.

The activities contribute to the achievement of **SDG 2** _(Zero Hunger)_, **SDG 9** _(Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure)_, and **SDG 13** _(Climate Action)_ — aligned with Smartagri's research direction, which focuses on precision agriculture technology innovation to support improved food security and agricultural production system efficiency.
